ideas.title: US Duty Price Sheet for UK Makers
ideas.summary: A saved catalog for UK handmade sellers who ship to the US through Folksy or their own shop, with confirmed US tariff codes that are recalculated into a US delivered-duty-paid price and Royal Mail postage table whenever a US rate change touches one of their products.

public.summary: Keep a US price and postage table for every product you make, and have it updated for you whenever US import duty changes.
public.problem: You make things in the UK and sell to US customers through Folksy or your own shop. Each product now needs its own US customs code, the import duty has to be paid up front and folded into your price or postage, and the rates keep changing. You work it all out once in a spreadsheet, then have to redo it by hand every time the rules move, or you give up on US buyers.
public.forWhom: Small UK makers who sell handmade goods to US customers through Folksy, Shopify or their own website and post with Royal Mail.
benefits: Each product's US code saved once and checked, with the official wording shown so you can confirm it
A US price and postage table you can copy into your shop
Your prices worked out again for you when a duty rate changes for something you sell
An email telling you which products changed and by how much
Fewer surprise charges and fewer parcels held up at the US border

ideas.problemStatement: Since US de minimis ended for mail and US orders must be sent duty-paid, UK makers who sell to the US outside Etsy (Folksy, which has flat postage profiles and no US price field, or their own Shopify Basic, Big Cartel or Squarespace shop) must find a US-specific 10-digit HTS code for each product (UK codes are not accepted), add the general duty plus the current country tariff layer, fold the total into a US price or Royal Mail postage band, and redo it whenever a rate changes. In their words: finding the right US codes 'is proving difficult' (a tote bag came out at 17.6% on top of 10%), one maker 'cannot find a suitable tariff code' and stopped offering US postage, and the makers who cope built their own spreadsheet mapping UK and US codes, duty, tariff and shipping, then recalculated their catalog by hand with free lookups. The one-off lookup is covered by free tools; the recurring recalculation of a whole catalog when rates change is not.
ideas.description: The maker builds a saved catalog (title, materials, origin, weight, current price) by hand or from a Folksy or Shopify CSV. For each product they confirm a US 10-digit HTS code, helped by a curated map of common handmade categories (jewellery, knitted and sewn textiles, ceramics, candles, cards, soft toys) and a search of the public USITC HTS data that shows the legal description and general rate. The app stacks the duty (general rate plus the current country-specific Chapter 99 layer, curated by hand with its source and date), applies Royal Mail DDP fees, and produces a US price and postage-band table per product. A nightly job watches the USITC release list and the curated Chapter 99 layer; when a change touches one of the maker's saved codes, it recalculates the affected prices and bands and emails the maker a before-and-after list. Exports are a Folksy-ready postage table, a Shopify product CSV and a plain CSV for Big Cartel or Squarespace.
ideas.targetCustomer: UK handmade sellers with roughly 10 to 300 products who ship to US buyers with Royal Mail DDP through Folksy or their own site (Shopify Basic without checkout duty collection, Big Cartel, Squarespace), including multi-channel makers who also sell on Etsy.
ideas.buyer: The maker, on a personal or business card, out of a very small software budget (typically a few pounds a month).
ideas.whyNow: US de minimis was suspended for mail and the CBP final rule of 2026-10-22 makes it indefinite with a new postal informal entry; Royal Mail warned of US partner-agency checks on regulated goods from 2026-10-22; Etsy made DDP mandatory for US orders from 2026-07-09 and gives its own sellers a free estimator, which leaves Folksy and own-site sellers to work it out themselves; and the USITC published 22 HTS revisions in 2026 up to 2026-10-30, so a once-off spreadsheet goes stale. The EU EUR 3 per-tariff-line duty on parcels under EUR 150 (from 2026-07-01) is a second, later market for the same recalculation engine.
ideas.founderFit: The core is careful data work Pisan can ship alone on his stack: a Flask job that syncs the free USITC HTS REST data into Supabase, a React table UI with CSV import and export, a curated mapping table, and a diff-and-recalculate job. No paid API is called at runtime. The hard part, keeping a maker-specific code map and tariff layer honest, is the kind of curated-dataset maintenance a CS educator does well; he has no UK maker network, so distribution leans on open online maker forums.

problemEvidence.author: Debbie Seton (thecrimsonrabbit)
problemEvidence.summary: One thread, counted as one item: Debbie Seton says the US requires its own codes and finding them 'is proving difficult' (a tote bag at 17.6% on top of 10%; 80% of her sales are to the US), but by 2026-07-27 she had recoded and repriced her catalog with a free Zonos account and ChatGPT, and her US channel is Etsy. Other commenters: Sarah Lou built her own UK/US code, duty, tariff and shipping spreadsheet that matched Royal Mail; Debby Coatham lacks time to recalculate GBP 34 bear postage; TheBeadHare saw a charge jump from 10% to 26%; PoppyKayDesigns argues Folksy gets very few US buyers. Context: the same author removed US shipping on Folksy in April 2026 because its postage profiles are clunky (https://talk.folksy.com/t/us-customs-tariffs-quick-question/33182).

problemEvidence.author: Jo Barnes (GINGERPINEAPPLECRAFTS)
problemEvidence.summary: One-sentence comment: stopped offering US postage because she cannot find a suitable tariff code, is confused by DDP, and the post office quoted much more than online. The thread was opened by Brenda Cumming on 2026-09-23 quoting Royal Mail's 2026-10-22 partner-agency checks for toys, cosmetics and children's products.

problemEvidence.author: Feemish
problemEvidence.summary: UK own-site seller using Royal Mail Click & Drop DDP finds Shopify checkout duties do not match Royal Mail's; a 2026-04-01 reply recommends full 10-digit US HTS codes per product and a 2026-08-05 reply notes the 2026-07-24 tariff change and the 2026-10-22 Chapter 99 compliance date. Older than 90 days.

problemEvidence.author: PourAway
problemEvidence.summary: UK seller pausing US shipping because Shopify stacked HS-code duty on top of the 10% tariff while Royal Mail postal shipments paid a different amount. Merchant complaints run 2025-08-31 to 2025-09-05 and concern a Shopify checkout bug; the 2026 replies are by developers and a researcher, not merchants.

problemEvidence.author: U.S. Customs and Border Protection
problemEvidence.summary: Final rule: de minimis indefinitely suspended for mail with a new postal informal entry; formal-entry compliance for mail subject to partner-agency requirements or Chapter 98/99 duties extended to 2027-01-20 (signal agent fetch).

problemEvidence.author: Liz Morton
problemEvidence.summary: Etsy requires non-US sellers to ship US orders DDP and build duties into prices from 2026-07-09, and offers a free US tariffs estimator in Shop Manager with separate US listing prices; relevant here because multi-channel makers must keep Folksy and own-site US prices consistent with it.

problemEvidence.author: European Commission
problemEvidence.summary: EU EUR 3 customs duty per tariff line on parcels up to EUR 150 from 2026-07-01 (signal agent fetch); the basis for a phase 2 EU sheet, not the MVP.

problemEvidence.author: US Tariff Rates (developer)
problemEvidence.summary: DutyCalc, a paid Shopify app for HS/HTS gaps and US tariff exposure: Free 10 lookups, Pro $49/month, Team $199/month; 0 reviews.

competitors.gap: Estimates US duty per listing, prompts HS-code review, was updated after the August 2026 rate change and works with US-specific listing prices, so it replaces this product for Etsy-only sellers; it does nothing for Folksy or own-site prices and postage.

competitors.name: Zonos free cross-border tools
competitors.price: Free with a Zonos account, per a maker's 2026-07-27 forum post (the page itself states no free tier)
competitors.gap: HS code calculator, duty and tax calculator and restricted-items lookup cover one-off lookups on any channel and partly cover regulated-goods checks; no saved catalog, no postage-band table and no recalculation when a rate changes.

competitors.price: 1,000 free classifications for a Zonos account (stated as intended for small businesses); paid subscriptions from 500 USD for 10,000 classifications
competitors.gap: Strong free code lookup; does not produce a Royal Mail DDP price and postage table or alert a maker when a saved code's rate changes.

competitors.name: The maker's own spreadsheet with free lookups
competitors.price: Free; about two days of the maker's time per full recode
competitors.gap: Works once, as Sarah Lou and Debbie Seton showed, but has to be redone by hand at every rate change and nobody tells the maker which products are affected.

competitors.gap: Shopify-only data-completeness fixer; does not compute a DDP price or postage table.

competitors.price: Free 20 SKUs/month, $9.90/month, $29/month (per the developer's forum post)
competitors.gap: Shopify-only; developer says rates are updated manually and estimates can overstate; aimed at importers, not maker pricing.

competitors.name: DutyCalc
competitors.gap: Shopify-only US tariff exposure for importers; no maker category map, postage table or Folksy export.

competitors.name: HClassify (LandedCost.io)

keyFeatures: Saved catalog with a confirmed US 10-digit HTS code per product, helped by a curated handmade-category map and checked against the live USITC record
Duty stack per product: general rate plus the current Chapter 99 country layer, with source and date shown
US DDP price and Royal Mail postage-band table per product
Automatic recalculation when a USITC revision or Chapter 99 change touches a saved code, with a before-and-after email
Exports: Folksy postage table, Shopify product CSV, plain CSV for Big Cartel and Squarespace
Simple warning for categories the US checks more closely (toys, children's products, cosmetics, food)

features: Manual or CSV product entry (title, material, origin, weight, price) from Folksy or Shopify
Curated map for about 40 common handmade categories with HTS search fallback, maker confirms each code
Duty stack and US DDP price per product for UK-origin goods
Royal Mail DDP postage-band table
Nightly check of the USITC release list and curated Chapter 99 layer, recalculation of affected products and an email listing the changes
CSV and Folksy-table export
outOfScope: Etsy listings and Etsy API write-back (Etsy's free estimator already covers Etsy-only sellers)
EU EUR 3 per-line duty sheet (phase 2)
Carriers beyond Royal Mail
Detailed partner-agency guidance beyond a category warning
AI classification of free text
mvpScope.buildEstimate: 3 to 4 weeks, most of it curating and testing the category map, the Chapter 99 layer and the change-detection job

ideas.techStack: React + Vite, Tailwind, Flask (nightly USITC HTS sync and release diff from the public no-key reststop endpoints), Supabase (products, curated map, rate snapshots, change log), transactional email. No paid API at runtime.

pricing.model: Per-shop subscription with a small free tier
pricing.pricePoint: GBP 4/month or GBP 36/year; free for up to 5 products
pricing.rationale: Below the cheapest Shopify tariff apps ($7.99 to $49/month) because makers are price-sensitive and free tools (Etsy's estimator, Zonos lookups) cover the one-off lookup; the paid value is the saved catalog and the automatic recalculation and alert when a rate changes, which free tools do not do.

ideas.revenueSketch: Illustrative estimate only: each 100 paying makers x GBP 36/year = GBP 3,600/year. The number of UK makers who still ship to the US through Folksy or their own site is unknown; the earlier 250-maker assumption included Etsy-only sellers, who are now out of scope, and one Folksy maker argues the site gets very few US buyers.
ideas.distribution: Answer threads and post a free code-and-price checker on talk.folksy.com (makers there already share spreadsheets and ask each other for codes), the Shopify Community UK duty threads for own-site sellers, and UK maker newsletters (Crafts Council Makers Manual readers); free tier for 5 products as the hook. Etsy seller groups are reached only for multi-channel makers.

validationTest.method: Publish a free one-page US duty and DDP price checker for 10 common handmade categories that shows what happened to each price at the last rate change, post it in the Folksy US-tariff threads and two Shopify Community UK duty threads, ask each user which channels they sell to the US through, and offer a GBP 36/year early-bird for the saved catalog with automatic recalculation and alerts.
validationTest.successCriteria: At least 10 paid early-bird sign-ups within 3 weeks from makers who sell to the US through Folksy or their own site (not Etsy only); Etsy-only sign-ups are not counted.
validationTest.cost: About 4 days of build time; no money beyond hosting.

ideas.moat: Weak. A curated, maintained map from maker product language to US HTS codes and duty layers, with a change history per code, and the per-maker catalog that makes recalculation automatic; Etsy and Zonos could extend their free tools to other channels.
compliance: Customs advice: estimates only, not a binding ruling; show the HTS legal text and tell the maker they remain responsible for the declared code (US classification responsibility sits with the importer; the maker acts as importer on DDP).
UK GDPR: store only seller account and product data; no buyer PII.
Accuracy and liability: terms of service limiting liability; show data date and revision on every figure and in every change email.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the table UI.

risks.risk: Makers solve it themselves once with free tools: the lead complainant recoded and repriced her catalog with a free Zonos account and ChatGPT in about two days.
risks.mitigation: Sell the recurring part, not the lookup: recalculation and a change email at every rate change, which the free tools and a spreadsheet do not give.

risks.risk: The non-Etsy segment may be small: one Folksy maker says Folksy gets very few US buyers, and there have been no new Folksy tariff posts since 2026-09-26.
risks.mitigation: Count only Folksy and own-site sign-ups in the validation test, and stop before building if fewer than 10 pay.

risks.risk: Free tools close the gap: Etsy's estimator is free and current, and Zonos offers free lookups.
risks.mitigation: Stay off Etsy-only sellers and focus on Folksy and own-site prices, the saved catalog and rate-change alerts.

risks.risk: The Chapter 99 tariff layer for UK goods changes often and sources conflict.
risks.mitigation: Curate the layer by hand from Federal Register and USITC notices, show the source and date, and alert on each USITC revision.

risks.risk: A wrong code costs the maker money or a held parcel.
risks.mitigation: Present codes as suggestions with legal text, require the maker to confirm each one, never auto-apply, keep a disclaimer.

scoreRationale.pain: Two independent recent Folksy items, one thread each (https://talk.folksy.com/t/33500.json, 2026-07-25; https://talk.folksy.com/t/33742.json, 2026-09-25), plus 2025 UK own-site complaints (https://community.shopify.com/t/usa-import-tariffs-and-end-of-de-minimis/567439); 4 not 5 because the lead complainant fixed it with free tools in two days and no new Folksy tariff posts appeared after 2026-09-26 (https://talk.folksy.com/search.json?q=tariff%20after%3A2026-09-26).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Paid tools for the task exist but with almost no reviews: DutyCalc $49/month (https://apps.shopify.com/dutycalc), Origova $7.99-$14.99/month (https://apps.shopify.com/origova); no freelancer jobs found (https://www.freelancer.com/api/projects/0.1/projects/active/?query=customs&limit=20&full_description=true), and makers lean on free lookups and spreadsheets (https://talk.folksy.com/t/33500.json).
scoreRationale.reachability: Folksy makers ask each other for codes and share spreadsheets in an open Discourse forum (https://talk.folksy.com/t/33500.json) and UK own-site sellers post in Shopify Community duty threads (https://community.shopify.com/t/usa-import-tariffs-and-end-of-de-minimis/567439); self-serve channels, but Pisan has no UK maker network and the non-Etsy pool is smaller.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Etsy's free Shop Manager calculator, kept current through the August 2026 change, replaces this for Etsy-only sellers (https://community.etsy.com/forum/announcements-290/topic/updated-sep-9-navigating-evolving-global-tariff-policies-22351/) and Zonos's free tools cover one-off lookups (https://zonos.com/cross-border-ecommerce-tools-calculators); the gap left is Folksy and own-site prices, saved-catalog recalculation and rate-change alerts.
scoreRationale.feasibility: The USITC HTS REST endpoints answer without a key (https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/releaseList lists 22 revisions in 2026; https://hts.usitc.gov/reststop/search?keyword=tote%20bag returns codes and general rates), but the Chapter 99 layer and handmade category map must be curated by hand; dropping Etsy write-back removes the Commercial Access review.
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: No buyer PII; the main burden is accuracy and a disclaimer that the maker owns the declared code as importer on duty-paid mail now that de minimis is suspended (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/22/2026-21600/indefinite-suspension-of-the-de-minimis-exemption-for-mail-shipments-and-new-postal-informal-entry).

review.findings: The reviewer fetched three Folksy threads, two Shopify Community threads, the Etsy tariff announcement, the Value Added Resource DDP article and Zonos's free-tools page. Authors, dates and quoted figures match (the 17.6% tote, 80% of sales to the US, the GBP 34 bears, Jo Barnes on 2026-09-25). Under the one-thread-one-item rule the Folksy pain is two independent items; thread 33182 shares an author with 33500 and is now context only. The lead complainant's US channel is Etsy, and two days later she had recoded her catalog with a free Zonos account and ChatGPT. Etsy's free calculator, kept current through the August 2026 changes, plus US-specific listing prices, replaces this product for Etsy-only sellers, and Zonos's free lookups cover one-off checks on any channel. The 2026 replies in Shopify UK thread 562214 are by developers, so it is dated 2025 and no longer called active; the Canadian complaint (672240) is a different customer whose problem was solved on 2026-08-31 and was dropped, as was the Etsy-only Mumsnet thread. Score change: pain 5 -> 4, total 22 -> 21; competitiveGap stays 2 but narrows. The idea is re-scoped to Folksy and own-site UK makers and to automatic recalculation of a saved catalog when rates change, and ships as provisional.

gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest's paid early-bird offer closes it: at least 10 paid GBP 36/year sign-ups within 3 weeks from makers who sell to the US through Folksy or their own site (not Etsy only) would show payment for the recalculation gap, raising willingnessToPay to 4 and the total to 22, which promotes the idea to validated.

ideas.title: Sync Switch Pre-flight for Etsy and Shopify Sellers
ideas.summary: For Etsy-and-Shopify sellers switching sync apps whose listings have missing or inconsistent SKUs: a one-time CSV pre-flight that pairs the two catalogs, hands back SKU-fix files for both stores so the next app links instead of duplicating, and saves a dated copy of the Etsy shop before the old app is uninstalled.

public.summary: Before you change the app that keeps your Etsy shop and Shopify store in step, this matches your listings across both, gives you the code fixes to make them line up, and saves a dated copy of your Etsy shop.
public.problem: You sell the same pieces on Etsy and on your Shopify store, and the app that keeps them in step is letting you down, so you want to change it. But the new app can only pair items that carry the same product code in both shops, and yours are missing or don't agree, so it either makes duplicates or leaves you matching hundreds of items by hand. And you have heard of shops losing dozens of Etsy listings the moment the old app was removed.
public.forWhom: Makers, crafters and vintage sellers with dozens or hundreds of items listed on both Etsy and Shopify who are about to change the app that links them.
benefits: See which Etsy and Shopify items belong together, even when their product codes are missing or different
Get ready-to-use files that give each matching pair the same code in both shops
Let your new app link existing listings instead of creating duplicates
Keep a dated copy of your Etsy listings and photos before removing the old app
Skip hours of matching items by hand

ideas.problemStatement: Sellers leaving one Etsy-Shopify sync app for another find that every app links existing listings only by matching SKUs; when SKUs are missing or inconsistent, setup republishes everything as duplicates or tells them to spend hours hand-matching SKUs and variant names (DPL's own reply says sync works only when SKUs are aligned), and resets or uninstalls of the old app have rewritten Etsy SKUs on 1,600 listings or deleted 50+ Etsy listings, with no copy to restore from.
ideas.description: The seller uploads two exports: Etsy's listing CSV and Shopify's product or inventory CSV. The tool pairs listings across the two where SKUs are missing or inconsistent, using normalized title, option values, price and a perceptual hash of the first photo (downloaded from the image URLs in the exports), and shows a match table with a confidence score and the unmatched leftovers on each side for the seller to confirm. It then outputs a SKU-fix CSV for each store's bulk editing route, giving every confirmed pair one shared SKU, so whichever sync app is installed next links the listings instead of duplicating them. It also bundles a dated Etsy-side archive (the listing CSV plus every downloaded photo) to keep before the old app is uninstalled. It is CSV-only and never connects to or writes to either store; a free preview shows how many listings it can pair, and the SKU-fix files and archive are a one-time purchase.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo makers and small craft or vintage shops with 50 or more listings on both Etsy and Shopify that lack consistent SKUs, at the moment they are leaving CedCommerce, DPL or Shopify's Marketplace Connect for another sync app.
ideas.buyer: The shop owner, as a one-time card purchase at the moment of switching apps, from the same budget that pays $9-$60/month for a sync app.
ideas.whyNow: Shopify stopped new Etsy connections in Marketplace Connect and froze its development after Etsy made readiness_state mandatory on 2025-09-30 (https://community.shopify.com/t/marketplace-connect-and-etsy/568436.json), so sellers moved to third-party sync apps and, per 2026 reviews, are now switching between them: CedCommerce reviewers in Jul-Oct 2026 report reset-rewritten SKUs, listings deleted on uninstall and moves to cheaper apps (https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-marketplace-integration/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest), and a DPL reviewer in September 2026 was told to hand-match SKUs before linking (https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-integration-dpl/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest). Each switch is a moment when SKUs must line up.
ideas.founderFit: The core is CSV parsing, fuzzy record matching and image hashing, which fits Pisan's Flask stack and his data/algorithms background; it is CSV-only and read-only, so there is no API approval to wait for and little support load. He has no network among Etsy sellers, so distribution must be self-serve.

problemEvidence.author: Be Lusch (Australia)
problemEvidence.summary: Paid CedCommerce for 2 years; 6 months of stock drift, and uninstalling deleted 50+ Etsy listings; now on a cheaper app. The date is an edit date, so the original post may be older. Same page (one item): LA Balloons (2026-07-29, 1,600 listings, a reset rewrote Etsy SKUs), Only Little Once (2026-08-24, paid $5,000 for an enterprise plan, switched to a cheaper competitor) and 5 Hearts Paper (2026-10-20, would pay $59/mo for a sync that worked, which is willingness to pay for sync, not for this tool).

keyFeatures: Upload Etsy's listing CSV and Shopify's product or inventory CSV; no store connection
Matching where SKUs are missing or inconsistent: normalized title, option values, price and first-photo perceptual hash, with a confidence score and unmatched lists on both sides
Free preview of how many listings pair up before paying
SKU-fix CSVs for both stores' bulk editors, giving each confirmed pair one shared SKU so the next sync app links instead of duplicating
Dated Etsy-side archive (listing CSV plus downloaded photos) as a zip, to keep before the old app is uninstalled

features: Upload both CSVs; fuzzy match by title, options, price and photo hash; editable match table
Download a Shopify SKU-fix CSV and an Etsy SKU-fix CSV for the confirmed pairs
Download a dated Etsy archive zip (CSV plus images fetched from the export's image URLs)
One-time checkout that unlocks the downloads after a free match-count preview
outOfScope: Any API connection to Etsy or Shopify (deferred; an Etsy key depends on a manually reviewed, currently unpredictable approval process)
Shopify-side snapshots (free Shopify backup apps already do this)
Daily drift alerts and ongoing monitoring (a working sync app prevents drift, and alerts need an Etsy API key)
Any writing to either store, order sync, and other marketplaces
mvpScope.buildEstimate: One weekend for the CSV-only version (upload, match, SKU-fix CSVs, Etsy archive zip, checkout); API connections deferred.

ideas.techStack: Single Flask app with server-rendered upload and match-table pages; pandas for CSV parsing, rapidfuzz for title/option matching, imagehash plus Pillow for photo hashes; Stripe Checkout for the one-time purchase; uploads and generated files held only for the session and deleted after download, so no database is needed. No Etsy or Shopify API and no paid API at runtime.

pricing.model: One-time pre-flight pack per store pair, with a free match-count preview
pricing.rationale: Sellers already pay $9-$60/month for the sync app itself (CedCommerce, DPL, Shuttle, SP); a one-time fee at the moment of switching is easy to weigh against hours of hand-matching or lost listings. It must beat a free alternative (SP's SKU linking plus a manual SKU pass), so the free preview has to show matches SP would miss; whether sellers pay $29 for that is unverified.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate only: 40 pre-flight packs/month x $29 = $1,160/month, with no recurring revenue. Assumes a steady stream of sellers switching sync apps (CedCommerce, DPL, Shuttle and shopUpz together carry about 2,600 reviews) and that the free preview converts about 5% of users; the number of sellers switching each month is unknown.
ideas.distribution: Self-serve. A free match-count preview page aimed at searches like 'Etsy Shopify duplicate listings' and 'match Etsy listings to Shopify without SKUs'; disclosed-developer replies in community.shopify.com Etsy-integration threads such as https://community.shopify.com/t/marketplace-connect-and-etsy/568436.json; Etsy-seller Facebook groups and YouTube creators who make Etsy-to-Shopify setup videos. First 10 customers: sellers posting about leaving CedCommerce or DPL, reached through those threads and the free preview.

validationTest.method: Build the CSV-only pre-flight in one weekend with a free match-count preview and a $29 checkout for the SKU-fix CSVs and Etsy archive; post it in 3 Etsy-integration threads on community.shopify.com and 2 Etsy-seller groups; ask every buyer whether they had first tried SP's free SKU linking or Shuttle's auto-match and how many listings those left unmatched.
validationTest.successCriteria: In 3 weeks: 40 sellers run the free preview and 5 buy the $29 pack through those threads and groups, and at least 3 buyers say the free SKU linkers left 50+ listings unmatched. Fewer than 2 sales, or buyers who say SP's free linking plus a manual pass was enough, means drop it.
validationTest.cost: One weekend of build, $0-$20 hosting, no ad spend.

ideas.moat: Weak. Any sync vendor (SP, DPL, Shuttle) could add fuzzy title and photo matching to its linker, and a developer in the Marketplace Connect thread is already pitching pre-migration SKU checks (https://community.shopify.com/t/marketplace-connect-and-etsy/568436.json). The only defensible part is being app-neutral at the moment of switching and having matching tuned on real handmade and vintage catalogs (one-of-a-kind items, inconsistent SKUs).
compliance: No API use in the MVP, so Etsy app approval and Etsy API terms do not apply yet; if API connections are added later, serving other sellers needs a Personal App and manually reviewed Commercial Access (https://developers.etsy.com/documentation/), and the Etsy API Terms of Use (HTTP 403 this run) must be read first.
Trademark: the product name names Etsy and Shopify descriptively and does not lead with 'Etsy'; check both companies' trademark-use guidance before launch (not checked this run).
Data: catalog data and the seller's own product photos only, no order or customer data; delete uploads and generated files after download and say so on the page.

Etsy policy risk: Etsy has deactivated listings tied to some third-party integration apps (2023, https://valueaddedresource.net/etsy-item-deactivations-shopify-integration-apps); a CSV-only tool that never touches the store is lower risk.

risks.risk: SP's free 'Smart SKU Linking' (https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-import-and-sync-by-sp) or Shuttle's auto-match plus a manual SKU pass is good enough, so sellers will not pay $29.
risks.mitigation: The free preview shows how many listings it pairs that have no matching SKU; the validation test asks buyers what the free linkers left unmatched, and the idea is dropped if the answer is 'nothing much'.

risks.risk: Etsy's listing CSV covers active listings only and its help page lists no variation columns (https://help.etsy.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000343508-How-to-Download-Your-Listing-Information), so variation-level SKU fixes on the Etsy side may be incomplete, and the archive misses inactive listings.
risks.mitigation: Use Shopify's variant-level export (https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/inventory/setup/inventory-csv) as the reference side, flag Etsy listings whose variations cannot be resolved, and state plainly that the archive covers active listings.

risks.risk: Whether Etsy's own tools can import a SKU-fix CSV was not checked; the Etsy-side file may have to be applied by hand or through the new sync app.
risks.mitigation: Order the Etsy-side file by listing title as it appears in Shop Manager, and check before launch which sync apps accept a SKU-mapping import.

risks.risk: An archive cannot bring back an Etsy listing's reviews, sales history or listing ID; sellers may expect a one-click restore.
risks.mitigation: Call it an archive for guided re-creation, and sell the SKU alignment (which avoids the destructive uninstall path) as the main value.

risks.risk: Crowding: two developers are building Etsy-Shopify tools in the same Shopify Community thread, one pitching pre-migration SKU checks (https://community.shopify.com/t/marketplace-connect-and-etsy/568436.json).
risks.mitigation: Ship the weekend version first and validate quickly; if a sync vendor adds fuzzy matching, stop rather than compete.

risks.risk: One-time revenue per seller with no recurring plan.
risks.mitigation: Treat it as a small, low-maintenance product; revisit monitoring only if an Etsy key becomes reliably obtainable.

scoreRationale.pain: Independent, recent complaints from paying merchants on separate pages: a seller told to hand-match SKUs and variant names to avoid duplicates (Apokrypha 2026-09-08, https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-integration-dpl/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest), and a reset that rewrote Etsy SKUs on 1,600 listings plus 50+ Etsy listings deleted on uninstall (LA Balloons 2026-07-29, Be Lusch edited 2026-09-16, https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-marketplace-integration/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest).
scoreRationale.willingnessToPay: Sellers pay $9-$59/mo for CedCommerce (1,248 ratings, https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-marketplace-integration) and $19.99-$59.99/mo for DPL (966 ratings, https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-integration-dpl), and one reviewer paid $5,000 for an enterprise plan (https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-marketplace-integration/reviews?ratings%5B%5D=1&ratings%5B%5D=2&sort_by=newest); at the low edge of 4 because this is a second purchase beside the sync app and the observed behaviour is switching apps.
scoreRationale.reachability: Self-serve but unproven: Shopify Community Etsy-integration threads exist (https://community.shopify.com/t/marketplace-connect-and-etsy/568436.json) and a free preview can rank on search, but Pisan has no network among Etsy sellers and Etsy's own forum threads sit behind a login.
scoreRationale.competitiveGap: Most of the job is served: SP matches existing listings by SKU for free (https://apps.shopify.com/etsy-import-and-sync-by-sp), Shuttle has free-tier SKU auto-match (https://apps.shopify.com/shuttle-transfer-from-etsy), StoreArk backs up Shopify free (https://apps.shopify.com/storeark), BackupShop.io sells Etsy backups (https://saasbrowser.com/saas/118418/backupshop) and developers are pitching pre-migration SKU checks (https://community.shopify.com/t/marketplace-connect-and-etsy/568436.json); only no-SKU matching plus an Etsy archive at switch time is left.
scoreRationale.feasibility: The CSV-only version is a one-weekend build with no API key, but Etsy's export lists no variation columns and covers active listings only (https://help.etsy.com/hc/en-us/articles/360000343508-How-to-Download-Your-Listing-Information), so match quality on variation listings is unproven, and any later API version waits on Etsy's unpredictable key approvals (https://github.com/etsy/open-api/discussions/1607).
scoreRationale.complianceBurden: CSV-only, catalog data only, no customer or order data and no store access; not 5 because Etsy has acted against integration apps before (https://valueaddedresource.net/etsy-item-deactivations-shopify-integration-apps) and the Etsy API terms were not read.

review.findings: The reviewer re-fetched and verified the three app review pages. On CedCommerce, Be Lusch (Australia, edited 2026-09-16) reports 6 months of drift and 50+ Etsy listings deleted on uninstall, and 5 Hearts Paper (2026-10-20) would pay $59/mo for a sync that worked; on DPL, Apokrypha (2026-09-08) was told to hand-match SKUs and variant names; on shopUpz, Saint Violet Creative (2025-11-29) had an import delete all Shopify listings. All are real merchants, not developers. No free product does the whole job, but its parts are covered: SP's free plan auto-links existing listings by SKU, Shuttle has free-tier SKU auto-match, StoreArk gives free daily Shopify backups with a diff-preview restore, and BackupShop.io sells Etsy-side backups. The aggrieved CedCommerce users fixed things by switching to a cheaper, better sync app (Trunk is 95% 5-star). The Marketplace Connect thread cited for whyNow is genuine (badgerated, 2025-09-30/10-01) but now also holds two developers promoting pre-launch Etsy sync tools, one pitching a pre-migration SKU check. competitiveGap was rescored 3 to 2, total 21 to 20; it stays provisional. The idea was re-scoped from a matcher, two-store snapshot and drift monitor to a one-time, CSV-only 'switching sync apps' pre-flight: matching listings that lack consistent SKUs, SKU-fix CSVs for both stores, and an Etsy-side archive taken before the old app is uninstalled. Complexity is now Weekend MVP, with API connections deferred.

gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest closes it: 5 sellers buying the $29 pack through Shopify Community threads and seller groups would show a working self-serve channel (reachability 3 to 4), and at least 3 buyers reporting that SP's free SKU linking or Shuttle's auto-match left 50+ listings unmatched would confirm the gap (competitiveGap 2 to 3), taking the total to 22 and promoting it to validated.

ideas.title: Delivery Canary for Digital Shops
ideas.summary: For creators selling ebooks, patterns, presets and printables on Shopify: a watchdog that places a free tagged test order on a schedule and checks that the download email arrives, which Gmail folder it lands in (Inbox, Promotions or Spam), and that its link returns the right file, plus a free scan for paid digital orders that were never fulfilled.

public.summary: Places a test order in your shop on a schedule and tells you if your download email stops arriving, lands in spam, or links to a broken file.
public.problem: You sell files, so you assume that once someone pays, the download email goes out, reaches their inbox and the link works. When the email starts landing in spam or the link breaks, nothing warns you, and you hear about it from confused customers. Checking by hand means placing test orders yourself, which nobody keeps doing.
public.forWhom: Solo creators and small studios selling ebooks, sewing and knitting patterns, presets, templates, audio and printables from their own Shopify shop.
benefits: Know whether your download emails reach the inbox, the promotions tab or the spam folder
Catch broken or wrong download links before customers do
See paid orders that never got their download, ready to resend
A short summary of every check instead of placing test orders yourself

ideas.problemStatement: Shopify sellers of digital products rely on a delivery app (Shopify's free Digital Products app, Sky Pilot, Filemonk, BIG Digital Downloads) to email a working download link after payment, and nothing tells them when that email stops reaching buyers. The clearest recent pain is inbox placement: a Filemonk seller's download emails go to customers' spam or promotions and 'I've tried everything in terms of verification ... with no luck' (2026-09-14), and a Sky Pilot reviewer says 'emails go to customer's spam' (2026-06-26). Older and weaker reports cover broken links and stopped fulfilment on Shopify's rebuilt app (May 2026) and one disputed claim of six months without delivery on BIG Digital Downloads (2026-04-13). Shopify's help page says the download destination 'isn't monitored' and tells merchants to place a test order themselves.
ideas.description: The merchant installs a small Shopify app that reads orders (read_orders) and creates draft orders (write_draft_orders). On a schedule (weekly by default) it creates a 100%-discounted, tagged order for one canary product and sends it to a seed Gmail account the developer owns. The app reads that mailbox with the free Gmail API and records whether the delivery email arrived, how long it took, and whether Gmail filed it in Inbox, Promotions or Spam; it then follows the download link and compares file type, size and hash with a baseline. Separately, it scans real paid orders whose line items do not require shipping and flags any still unfulfilled after a grace period. Results go into a dashboard and a digest email, and canary orders are tagged and archived so they stay out of reports. Whether a draft order completed through the API triggers each delivery app is unverified; if it does not, the canary must instead go through a real checkout using a 100%-off code the merchant creates.
ideas.targetCustomer: Solo creators and micro studios selling digital files (patterns, ebooks, presets, templates, sample packs, printables) from their own Shopify store with a delivery app installed.
ideas.buyer: The shop owner, from the store's app budget on their own card (they already pay $9 to $55 a month for the delivery app).
ideas.whyNow: Shopify's free Digital Downloads app was rebuilt as 'Digital Products' in 2026 and drew a cluster of breakage reviews in May 2026; SendOwl's 2025 price rise pushed long-time sellers onto newer apps; and spam placement of download emails is still being reported on community.shopify.com in September 2026. Shopify's own docs tell merchants to verify delivery by placing test orders by hand, and a July 2026 community thread on catching checkout failures gets the same advice (periodic real test orders, or generic synthetic monitors), with no tool that checks the digital delivery email.
ideas.founderFit: Pisan's stack (React + Vite, Flask, Supabase) covers a Shopify embedded app plus a scheduler; the core is a deterministic end-to-end test harness, which is a testing problem a CS educator understands well. No paid API on his key at runtime: the Shopify Admin API is free, and the seed mailbox is his own Gmail account read with the free Gmail API.

problemEvidence.summary: Sky Pilot: 'emails go to customer's spam' (2026-06-26); a 9-year user says downloads 'regularly drop out', customers are disconnected partway and the seller is still billed for the bandwidth (2026-01-07).

Tied to one rebuild, and many of the page's low reviews are about UI changes.

competitors.name: Shopify Flow (unfulfilled-order summary template)
competitors.gap: Can email a list of paid orders still unfulfilled after N days for free, which covers the 'app stopped fulfilling' case, but cannot tell whether the email arrived, landed in spam, or whether the link opens the right file; apps that mark orders fulfilled when they send are invisible to it.

competitors.name: Shopify Digital Products app download log
competitors.gap: Logs downloads per order and can resend, but sends the merchant no alert on failure; the help page says the destination URL 'isn't monitored' and recommends placing a test order by hand. Only covers Shopify's own app.

competitors.name: The delivery apps themselves (Sky Pilot, Filemonk, BIG Digital Downloads, SendOwl; also MP Digital Downloads, GIT, FileFlow)
competitors.price: Sky Pilot free / $9 / $24.99 / $54.99 per month; Filemonk free / $10 / $25; BIG $9.99 / $19.99; SendOwl $39 / $87 / $159; others unknown
competitors.gap: Each shows its own logs and can resend, but none reports whether its email reached the buyer's inbox or spam, and nobody checks the app from outside.

competitors.name: CheckoutGuard
competitors.gap: Alerts on drops in order volume; does not test the delivery email, its inbox placement or its download link.

competitors.name: Generic synthetic monitors (Pingdom, Checkly)
competitors.gap: Recommended in a community thread for catching checkout failures, but they script page checks, not a Shopify order followed by a delivery email and a per-order download link.

competitors.name: LinkFix
competitors.price: Free for 3 links; $19 one-time lifetime deal for the first 50 customers; subscription price not stated
competitors.gap: Pings static public URLs every 5 minutes; cannot test per-order tokenised download links, email delivery, or spam placement, and does not read Shopify orders.

competitors.name: LateKit: Late Shipment Alerts (and parcel monitors such as Delivery-Radar, ShipAware)
competitors.gap: Built for physical parcels and carrier delays, not file delivery.

competitors.name: SLA Guard Fulfillment Alerts

keyFeatures: Scheduled canary order: a free, tagged order for one product, delivered to a seed Gmail mailbox
Inbox placement: whether the delivery email landed in Inbox, Promotions or Spam, and how long it took to arrive
Link test: follows the download link and compares file type, size and hash with the baseline
Real-order watch: paid orders with non-shipping items still unfulfilled after a grace period, with a jump to resend
Digest email plus an instant alert when a canary fails or lands in spam

features: Shopify app with read_orders and write_draft_orders; Level 1 protected customer data only (no customer names or emails read)
Weekly canary order on one product, tagged and archived after the run (draft-order route if the dev-store check passes, otherwise a real checkout with a merchant-created 100%-off code)
Seed Gmail mailbox owned by the developer, read with the free Gmail API: arrival time and Inbox/Promotions/Spam placement
Download-link extraction for Shopify Digital Products, Sky Pilot and Filemonk emails, with a file size and hash check
Unfulfilled digital order scan and a digest email
outOfScope: Placement checks in Outlook, Yahoo or other mailbox providers
Bandwidth forecasting and license-key stock (no API exposes them for these apps)
WooCommerce and Etsy (Etsy delivers files itself)
Automatic resending of failed deliveries
mvpScope.buildEstimate: Estimate: 3 to 4 weeks including Shopify app review on the draft-order route; unknown if the dev-store check forces the real-checkout fallback

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind (Shopify embedded admin UI with App Bridge), Flask API, Supabase (Postgres + scheduled jobs), Shopify Admin GraphQL API, Gmail API on a developer-owned seed account; no paid API on the developer's key at runtime.

pricing.model: Monthly Shopify subscription via the Billing API
pricing.pricePoint: Free: unfulfilled digital order scan and a weekly canary (arrival and link check); $7/month: inbox placement, daily canary on up to 5 products, instant alerts
pricing.rationale: Must sit well below the delivery app it watches ($9.99-$54.99) and near LateKit ($3.99-$7.99); the free tier competes with Shopify Flow's free unfulfilled-order email, so the paid tier sells on inbox placement, the only check with a recent, independent complaint behind it.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate: if 1% of the roughly 3,300 merchants who have reviewed the five main delivery apps (882 + 1,444 + 441 + 508 + 39 reviews, used only as a scale proxy) convert, 33 x $7 = $231 MRR; 300 paying shops would be $2,100 MRR. Both are assumptions, not observed, and the low failure rate visible in reviews (BIG: 5 one-star of 882) suggests conversion may be lower.
ideas.distribution: Shopify App Store listing in the digital downloads category, plus direct, non-promotional answers to recurring community.shopify.com threads on download emails going to spam and links failing (where sellers like selenadaphne and HulkyZo post); then a co-marketing ask to a delivery app that wants an independent 'delivery verified' badge.

validationTest.method: Step 1, before anything else: on a Shopify dev store, complete a 100%-off draft order through the Admin API (draftOrderComplete, marked paid) for a product set up in each of Shopify Digital Products, Sky Pilot and Filemonk, and record whether each app sends its download email. If an app does not fire, repeat with a 100%-off discount code through a real checkout to confirm the fallback route. Step 2: run the canary by hand for 10 Shopify digital sellers recruited from community.shopify.com and pattern/preset seller groups (they create a 100%-off code, Pisan places a weekly test order to his seed Gmail account and reports arrival, Inbox/Promotions/Spam placement and link status), then ask each seller to prepay $7/month for the automated version.
validationTest.successCriteria: Step 1: draft-order canaries trigger delivery in at least 2 of the 3 apps (otherwise the build switches to the real-checkout route and compliance is re-checked before going further). Step 2: at least 3 of the 10 shops have a canary land in Spam or Promotions or hit a broken link or unfulfilled paid order within 4 weeks, and 4 of the 10 sellers prepay.
validationTest.cost: About 2 hours for the dev-store check and about 15 hours over 4 weeks for the hand-run canaries; $0 (dev store, free Gmail API).

ideas.moat: Thin. Per-app email parsers and an accumulated history of which delivery apps land in spam or fail, and how often, are the only assets; a delivery app could add self-tests. Independence (watching the app from outside, from a real mailbox) is the selling point a delivery app cannot claim about itself.
compliance: Shopify protected customer data: orders are protected data; staying at Level 1 (no name, email, address, phone fields) still needs review for a public app (https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/protected-customer-data).

Shopify App Store requirements have no rule on apps creating test orders, but 1.1.4 forbids falsified data that deceives merchants or buyers, so canaries must be merchant-consented, clearly tagged and archived (https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements). The real-checkout fallback, if needed, must be re-checked against these requirements.
Shopify mandatory GDPR webhooks (customers/data_request, customers/redact, shop/redact) and Billing API for charges.
Canary orders must be zero-value so they do not distort sales reports or tax filings; they count toward order caps on some delivery app plans (Filemonk free plan: 50 orders/month).
Gmail API is used only on the developer-owned seed account; no merchant or buyer mailbox is accessed.
Downloading the merchant's paid files to verify them: store only hashes and sizes, never the files.

risks.risk: Orders created by draftOrderComplete may not trigger some delivery apps the way a checkout does: the API page is silent, and a 2021 community report says a manually created 100%-off order marked paid did not send the download link in Shopify's old Digital Downloads app (https://community.shopify.com/t/can-manual-creation-of-orders-affect-digital-download-delivery/55046).
risks.mitigation: Step 1 of the validation test checks this on a dev store for Shopify Digital Products, Sky Pilot and Filemonk before any build; fall back to merchant-created 100%-off codes through a real checkout, and re-check compliance if so.

risks.risk: Delivery failures look rare (BIG: 5 one-star reviews out of 882), so many sellers may never see a failed canary and cancel.
risks.mitigation: Lead with inbox placement, which varies over time and gives every run a result worth reading, and measure fault rates in the hand-run test before building.

risks.risk: Placement in one seed Gmail account is a proxy, not what every buyer's mailbox does.
risks.mitigation: Say so in the report, show placement trends rather than single results, and add other providers only if sellers ask.

risks.risk: Shopify Flow's free unfulfilled-order email already covers the most common failure, so the paid tier must sell on link, file and spam checks.
risks.mitigation: Give the unfulfilled scan away free and price only the end-to-end checks.

risks.risk: Sellers react to a failure by switching delivery apps, not by buying monitoring (SendOwl and Sky Pilot reviewers did exactly that).
risks.mitigation: Position as the check that tells you when to switch, and pitch to sellers mid-migration.

risks.risk: Delivery email formats change and break the link parser.
risks.mitigation: Fall back to the order status page download block and alert on parse failure rather than reporting a false pass.

risks.risk: Each canary download consumes the merchant's bandwidth quota and download limits.
risks.mitigation: Use a small dedicated canary product file and weekly default cadence.

review.findings: Score change: pain 4 -> 3, total 20 -> 19; other scores unchanged. The reviewer fetched four evidence items: the BIG and Shopify Digital Products low-star review pages, and community threads 709826 and 681919. Authors and dates match, but the lindamae thread (709826) was misread: she attached a file to physical pre-sale products after customers had paid, so no delivery app failed, and it was dropped. SpineFit's 'six months without delivery' review is disputed in a founder reply that blames a product the merchant deleted, and BIG has only 5 one-star reviews out of 882. That leaves selenadaphne's spam complaint (2026-09-14) as the only one inside 90 days, so Gmail seed-inbox placement was moved from phase 2 into the MVP. No free or paid product runs end-to-end checks of digital delivery: Shopify Flow (unfulfilled orders), the delivery apps' own logs, CheckoutGuard (order-volume drops) and Pingdom/Checkly (generic synthetic monitoring) each cover only part of the job, so this is a rescore, not a kill. A 2021 community report that a manually created 100%-off paid order did not trigger the download email makes the draft-order mechanism the main build risk, so the dev-store check of it is now the first validation step. No rule in the Shopify App Store requirements forbids merchant-consented, tagged test orders, and nothing in ideas/index.jsonl duplicates the idea.

gateGap.closedBy: The hand-run canary in Step 2 of the validationTest closes the largest gap (pain): if at least 3 of the 10 shops have a canary land in Spam or Promotions or hit a broken link or unfulfilled paid order within 4 weeks, pain rises to 4, and if 4 of the 10 sellers prepay, willingnessToPay and reachability rise to 4. Together with Step 1 showing draft-order canaries trigger at least 2 of the 3 delivery apps (feasibility 4), the total reaches 23 and the idea can be promoted to validated. If Step 1 fails, the real-checkout route must be proven before Step 2 counts.

ideas.title: Deposits Register for Xero
ideas.summary: For event, travel and tour operators, creative studios and commission makers on Xero with no job or booking system: request a deposit with a reference before the final invoice exists, see every deposit held and how old it is, and apply it to the final invoice in one click.

public.summary: Keeps a clear list of every deposit you have asked for or taken in Xero, and takes each one off the final bill for you when the work is done.
public.problem: You take a deposit weeks or months before the trip, event or commission is finished, long before there is a final invoice to put it against. The money lands in your bank with nothing to match it to, so you keep a separate spreadsheet of who has paid, and you have to remember to knock each deposit off the final bill by hand. Miss one and a customer gets billed twice; lose track and you cannot say how much of your customers' money you are holding.
public.forWhom: Event, travel and tour businesses, creative studios and makers who work on commission, who keep their books in Xero and have no separate booking or job system.
benefits: Ask for a deposit with its own reference, so the payment is easy to match when it arrives
One list of every deposit you are owed, holding or have already used, with how long each has been waiting
Know at any moment how much of your customers' money you are holding
Deposits come off the final invoice in one click, so nobody is billed twice
Payment details go out from your own business, so customers can trust them

ideas.problemStatement: For businesses that take a deposit before the final invoice exists, Xero has no deposit record of its own: Xero's deposit request (rolled out May-June 2026) is Stripe-only and attaches to an invoice, and matching a part payment to an existing invoice is already free. So upfront bank-transfer payments 'sit in the unallocated banking transactions for weeks or months' (Mark Compton, 2026-08-10), deposits outstanding live in 'a spreadsheet to keep track of clients deposits outstanding' (Matthew Powell, 2026-08-05), the common workaround is 'a very complicated draft invoice then minus the payment which we have reconciled to Customer deposits' on orders that run up to 12 months (Keith Gatenby, 2026-08-05), deposits taken for future invoices do not appear in Aged Receivables (Kyle Hogan, 2026-05-25), and staff cannot tell whether a deposit was paid (Mel Greenwood, 2026-08-27).
ideas.description: A small web app connected to the business's Xero organisation, built around three things that matter only when the deposit arrives before the final invoice exists. (1) Deposit request: staff pick a contact, enter the booking or commission and the amount, and the app creates a deposit document in Xero (an authorised invoice coded to a Customer Deposits liability account, or a prepayment) with a unique reference; the payment details travel on the Xero invoice PDF or in an email sent from the business's own verified domain, never from a third-party sender. (2) Deposits Register: the app polls Xero for payments after the user reconciles (Xero's API does not expose unreconciled bank lines) and lists every deposit as requested, overdue, held or applied, with ageing and the total held as a liability. (3) Apply to final invoice: one click adds a 'Less deposit received' line against the liability account, or allocates the prepayment through the Prepayments Allocations endpoint, and marks the deposit applied so it cannot be used twice.
ideas.targetCustomer: Owners, office staff and outside bookkeepers at small Xero businesses (roughly 1 to 20 staff) in event, travel and tour operation, creative studios and commission making, that take deposits before the final invoice exists and have no vertical job or booking system. Trades and hire businesses are excluded: ServiceM8, Fergus/Tradify and HirePOS already handle deposits for them. Commenters are mostly AU, NZ and UK businesses; none identified as photographers or makers, so the creative-studio and maker segment is an assumption.
ideas.buyer: The business owner on the business card, or a bookkeeper on behalf of several client organisations in these verticals.
ideas.whyNow: Xero shipped Stripe-only deposits in May-June 2026 (admin response 2026-06-15 on the 515-vote idea), which put the deposit gap in front of every bank-transfer business at once, and Aug-Oct 2026 comments keep asking for it. Xero marked 'deposits without Stripe' In discovery on 2026-10-15, so collecting a deposit by bank transfer may soon be built in; the register of deposits held before an invoice exists and the apply-to-final-invoice step are what would remain. An Australian card-surcharge rule change (Monique Lennon, 2026-09-24) is pushing some businesses off card for deposits.
ideas.founderFit: A narrow CRUD app over a documented REST API (Xero Accounting API: Invoices, Payments, Prepayments, Allocations) fits React + Vite, Flask and Supabase; no paid API is called on Pisan's key at runtime. Pisan has no accounting-industry network and Xero's community rules out pitching in idea threads, so distribution is cold outreach to bookkeepers in these verticals and a search-ranked workaround guide: a weak fit, reflected in reachability 2.

mvpScope.buildEstimate: About 3 weekends for the MVP, plus Xero certification (needs real customers and a review), so several weeks before it can be offered beyond the free tier's 5 connections.

ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind front end, Flask API, Supabase (Postgres, auth) for deposit records and tokens; Xero Accounting API via OAuth 2.0; transactional email (e.g. Resend or SES) sending only from the customer's own verified domain. No paid API on the founder's key at runtime beyond email and hosting.

pricing.model: Per Xero organisation monthly subscription, with a bookkeeper bundle
pricing.pricePoint: US$12/month per organisation; US$60/month for up to 10 organisations
pricing.rationale: Below Quotient's US$28/month, which bundles deposits with quoting (https://www.quotientapp.com/pricing); the target has no job or booking tool and is not looking to adopt one. Must cover Xero's platform fee (Core A$35/month for 50 connections, Plus A$245/month for 1,000 connections and an App Store listing, https://developer.xero.com/pricing). Price acceptance is untested.

ideas.revenueSketch: Estimate only: 100 organisations x US$12/month = US$1,200 MRR, less about A$245/month for Xero's Plus tier once past 50 connections. Assumes bookkeeper referrals and a search-ranked guide page bring the customers; the number of Xero event, travel, studio and commission businesses taking deposits before invoicing is unknown.
ideas.distribution: First 10: cold outreach to bookkeepers whose sites list event, travel, tour or creative-industry clients, offering a free beta for their client organisations; a Xero-workaround guide page that aims to rank for searches like 'Xero customer deposits bank transfer' and explains the liability-account method, with a beta sign-up. In Xero's idea threads, at most one helpful, non-promotional answer explaining the workaround, because Xero's community guidelines forbid commercial posts (https://xero.com/us/support/community-guidelines) and UserVoice has no direct messages. The Xero App Store comes later, once certified and on the Plus tier (https://developer.xero.com/pricing).

validationTest.method: Publish the Xero-workaround guide page with a beta sign-up, email 30 bookkeepers who serve event, travel, tour or creative businesses, and run a free beta on Xero's Starter tier (5 connections, no fee); ask beta organisations to pre-pay US$12/month from month two.
validationTest.successCriteria: Within 4 weeks, 5 organisations in the target verticals connect, at least 2 of them through a bookkeeper, and each records at least 3 deposits taken before the final invoice existed; 3 of the 5 pre-pay; and Xero's 'deposits without Stripe' item has not moved beyond 'In discovery' when checked.
validationTest.cost: About 3 weekends of build plus a day of outreach; a domain, under US$50.

ideas.moat: Thin. The register and the apply step are easy to copy, and Xero may close part of the gap. Any edge comes from bookkeeper relationships in these verticals, certification, and the deposit history stored per organisation.
compliance: Xero Developer Platform: an app must be certified before it is offered to users (connection, scopes, error handling, data integrity, account and payment mapping, tax rates) with annual recertification (https://developer.xero.com/xero-developer-platform-commercial-terms)

Tax treatment of deposits differs by country (UK VAT tax point on receipt of a deposit; Australian GST on part-payments versus security deposits); let the user choose the account and tax rate, and have an accountant review the default setup
Financial and customer personal data: GDPR/UK GDPR and the Australian Privacy Act; request minimal scopes, encrypt tokens, delete data on disconnect
Payment details in email: send only from the business's own authenticated domain (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) or via Xero's invoice email, to avoid looking like payment-redirection fraud
The app writes to the customer's ledger: every write must be reversible and logged
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA for the dashboard and the customer-facing request page

risks.risk: Emailing bank details from a third-party sending domain looks like payment-redirection (invoice) fraud to customers, so deposit requests get ignored or reported, and a compromised account could be used to change bank details.
risks.mitigation: Never send payment details from the app's own domain: put them on the Xero invoice PDF and send through Xero, or send from the business's own verified domain; lock bank details after setup and require re-authentication and an alert to the owner to change them.

risks.risk: Xero ships bank-transfer deposits ('deposits without Stripe' is In discovery as of 2026-10-15).
risks.mitigation: Do not lead with 'request a deposit by bank transfer'; the product is the register of deposits held before an invoice exists and the apply step, which a request feature does not cover. Validate before building and keep build cost to a few weekends.

risks.risk: Free workarounds are good enough: matching a part payment to an existing invoice, or footer bank details plus split reconciliation.
risks.mitigation: Target only businesses that take deposits before the final invoice exists and hold many at once (events, travel, commissions), where the spreadsheet is the pain; drop prospects who invoice up front.

risks.risk: Vertical job and booking tools (ServiceM8, Fergus/Tradify, HirePOS) already handle deposits, and more may add it for events or travel.
risks.mitigation: Exclude trades and hire; screen beta users for having no job or booking system.

risks.risk: Weak channel: Xero's community guidelines forbid commercial posts, UserVoice has no direct messages, the App Store needs certification and the Plus tier, and Pisan has no bookkeeper network.
risks.mitigation: Cold outreach to bookkeepers in these verticals plus the search-ranked guide page; the validation test measures whether either brings organisations before any build beyond the beta.

risks.risk: Xero's API does not expose unreconciled bank statement lines, and Xero has said it has no plans to add reconciliation to the API (admin reply 2026-09-02).
risks.mitigation: Rely on Xero's reconciliation suggesting the deposit invoice by amount and reference; the app reads payments only after the user reconciles.

risks.risk: Wrong accounting treatment (income vs liability, tax) damages trust with bookkeepers.
risks.mitigation: Offer liability-invoice and prepayment modes, make the account and tax rate explicit settings, and recruit a bookkeeper adviser in the beta.

scoreRationale.competitiveGap: 3: no tool keeps a register of deposits taken before the invoice exists for businesses without a job or booking system, but ServiceM8 Pay (https://support.servicem8.com/hc/en-us/articles/10804448488463-How-Deposits-sync-to-Xero-with-ServiceM8-Pay) and HirePOS (https://docs.hirepos.com/en/articles/4332353) cover trades and hire, free matching covers deposits against existing invoices, and Xero's non-Stripe deposits are In discovery (https://productideas.xero.com/forums/967115-invoices-quotes/suggestions/51108952-invoice-ability-to-use-deposits-without-stripe).

review.findings: Reachability lowered 3 -> 2, total 19 -> 18 (pain 4, willingnessToPay 3, competitiveGap 3, feasibility 3, complianceBurden 3 unchanged); still provisional. The reviewer re-fetched the 515-, 259- and 44-vote threads and the quotes, authors and dates hold up: Mark Compton (2026-08-10) on up-front bank-transfer payments sitting unallocated 'for weeks or months', Matthew Powell (2026-08-05) on a deposits spreadsheet, Keith Gatenby (2026-08-05) on a 'very complicated draft invoice then minus the payment' reconciled to Customer deposits (reworded from 'negative draft invoice'; the Scarlett AI comment was dropped), and Xero setting 'deposits without Stripe' to In discovery on 2026-10-15. None of the commenters is a developer promoting an app, so the draft's claim that developers already pitch in these threads was removed; Xero's community guidelines forbid commercial posts (https://xero.com/us/support/community-guidelines), which is why reachability fell and the thread-reply channel was replaced with bookkeeper outreach and a workaround guide page. The same threads show free workarounds (Andrew Syme: match any part payment to an unpaid invoice; Aaron Lowndes: bank details in the invoice footer plus split reconciliation), and paid vertical tools (ServiceM8 Pay, HirePOS; Preno and Workshop Software in search results) already sync deposits to Xero as prepayments. The idea was therefore narrowed to event, travel and tour operators, creative studios and commission makers with no job or booking system, and to the Deposits Register plus apply-to-final-invoice product, with a new payment-redirection-fraud risk. Not a duplicate of the 2026-11-05 Remittance Matcher (QuickBooks, lump-sum allocation) or the 2026-11-06 Recurring Invoice Send Check (silent recurring failures), though it shares the small-Xero-business customer with the latter.

gateGap.closedBy: The validationTest closes it, and needs 4 more points. Three of five target-vertical organisations pre-paying would lift willingnessToPay 3 -> 4; at least 2 of those organisations arriving through bookkeepers would show a repeatable channel and lift reachability 2 -> 4; and Xero's 'deposits without Stripe' item still not past 'In discovery', with beta users recording deposits taken before the final invoice existed, would support competitiveGap 3 -> 4. All three together reach 22 (pain 4, willingnessToPay 4, reachability 4, competitiveGap 4, feasibility 3, complianceBurden 3); anything less keeps it provisional.

runNotes.caveats: First run of 2026-11-08 (Sunday). Four provisional ideas ship (21, 20, 19, 18); none cleared the gate of 22. Six candidates were researched and adversarially reviewed: one killed (Square class waitlist and series: Square's API does not expose Classes, and Occasion already sells the buildable standalone version to Square studios) and five rescored down (US Duty Price Sheet 22 to 21, because the Folksy commenters are one thread and Etsy's free estimator covers Etsy-only sellers; listing matcher 21 to 20, because SP's free plan auto-links SKUs and StoreArk backs up Shopify free; Delivery Canary 20 to 19, because one evidence thread was misread and the lead review is disputed; Xero deposits 19 to 18, because Xero's community rules forbid promoting in idea threads; Balance Due 20 to 16, not shipped). Deposits Register for Xero (18) shipped over two unreviewed watchlist entries at 19 (Flat-Fee Text Personalizer, One-Off Hold Guard): it was selected at a preliminary 19, tied with them, on stronger complaint evidence (515, 259 and 44-vote Xero ideas with named 2026 comments), and lost a point in review. It is the third small-Xero-business idea in four days. Each idea is scoped to a different customer and problem, but all four sit in Small Business Ops territory; categories were spread (Accessibility & Compliance, Small Business Ops x2, Micro-SaaS). The focus source A12 (HN) yielded one first-person maker complaint in 15 queries; the lens is poorly served there. C10 yielded strong change events (Etsy DDP 2026-07-09, CBP de minimis rules, EU EUR 3 duty, Etsy photo rules, Pass+ shutdown, Patreon billing), but Pass+ and Squarespace complaints were only on Reddit, which is not counted. B11 (freelancer.com) found almost no task-specific paid jobs across about 60 queries; its search barely narrows. No tutor or working-photographer forum with business pain was found, so neither group is covered today. No watchlist entries carried over from 2026-11-07.
